title: MAP Sensor Circuit Fault
shortDescription: PGM-FI detected MAP sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription:
The MIL blinks once long then pauses. PGM-FI sees the Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor input outside the 0.5-4.5V operating range.

Common on CBR/Rebel/CRF bikes with sensor under tank. Causes include disconnected vacuum hose, open wiring, or failed sensor. Bike may run rich and idle poorly.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect MAP vacuum hose to throttle body.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Signal wire should read ~3V at idle with engine running.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap MAP, clear code by disconnecting battery 10 seconds.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 1 MAP sensor fix

faq.a: Jump service connector or observe MIL pattern after jumping DLC.

title: TPS Fault
shortDescription: Throttle Position Sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription:
MIL blinks five times. PGM-FI cannot calibrate throttle closed/open positions. Signal voltage should sweep 0.5V to 4.2V smoothly.

Caused by worn TPS wiper, dirty throttle body, or broken signal wire. Ride-by-wire bikes will enter limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Use throttle body cleaner with bike running.

fixSteps.title: Check TPS voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Slowly rotate throttle observing smooth voltage ramp.

fixSteps.title: Replace TPS
fixSteps.instruction: TPS usually non-serviceable — replace throttle body on modern bikes.

whenToCallPro: If ride-by-wire adaptation learn is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 5 TPS fix

faq.a: HDS tool for idle air adaptation on newer models.

title: Engine Coolant Temp Sensor Fault
shortDescription: ECT sensor signal out of plausible range.
fullDescription:
Blink 7 means ECT signal implausibly high or low. PGM-FI substitutes default for fueling which causes over-rich mixture and hot running.

Sensor mounts on cylinder head or radiator. Usually cheap to replace once located.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Clean ECT connector, apply dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Drain small amount of coolant, swap sensor.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 7 ECT sensor fix

faq.a: Short rides ok; cooling fan control may fail.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Blink 8 indicates no pulses from VSS. Speedo freezes and fueling strategies that depend on speed (lean angle, cruise control) are disabled.

Usually failed sensor, broken tone ring, or wiring. CBR-style mount on front sprocket cover is exposed to debris.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front sprocket cover, check for debris/damage.

fixSteps.title: Check air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor tip should be 0.7-1.2 mm from tone ring.

fixSteps.title: Replace VSS
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor and verify on road test.

whenToCallPro: Tone ring on output shaft means engine out.
videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 8 speed sensor fix

faq.a: Speed is used for closed-loop timing adjustments.

title: Intake Air Temp Sensor Fault
shortDescription: IAT sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription:
Blink 9 indicates IAT reading implausible. PGM-FI uses default 25C causing minor rich condition.

Air filter box sensors fail from heat cycling and oil vapor contamination. Inexpensive to swap.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Spray MAF-safe cleaner on IAT element, let dry.

fixSteps.title: Check resistance
fixSteps.instruction: At ambient ~2k ohms; changes with heat.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 9 IAT sensor fix

faq.q: Did over-oiling the filter cause it?
faq.a: Often yes — re-oil lightly per K&N spec.

title: Vehicle Speed/MAP Correlation Fault
shortDescription: Plausibility fault between VSS and MAP during operation.
fullDescription:
Blink 11 appears when ECM sees conflicting data — e.g. high load reported by MAP at zero speed over time. This can indicate disconnected vacuum hose on MAP or failed VSS.

Primarily on CBR/ VFR models with plausibility monitoring.

fixSteps.title: Verify VSS pulses
fixSteps.instruction: Jack up rear wheel, spin, check voltage pulses.

fixSteps.title: Clear and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Short circuit service connector to clear memory.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 11 plausibility fix

faq.a: Mild — fuel mapping slightly off, fix soon.

title: Injector #1 Fault
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Blink 12 indicates injector 1 coil resistance out of range or driver error. Cylinder won't receive fuel, causing severe misfire.

Honda inline-four owners often see this after carb-to-FI conversion attempts or harness damage during fairing removal.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Press injector connector until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Replace injector
fixSteps.instruction: Depressurize rail, swap injector, new o-rings.

whenToCallPro: Fuel system work is risky without training.
videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 12 injector fix

faq.q: Can I swap injectors to test?

title: O2 Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Oxygen sensor circuit not switching / stuck.
fullDescription:
Blink 13 logs when O2 does not cross stoichiometric threshold. PGM-FI reverts to open loop, reducing economy.

Common after aftermarket exhaust without O2 bung, leaks at header, or aged sensor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten header flange bolts, replace gaskets if leaking.

fixSteps.title: Replace O2
fixSteps.instruction: Install new OEM narrowband O2 with anti-seize on threads only.

fixSteps.title: Clear code
fixSteps.instruction: Short service connector or ride 5-10 miles to relearn.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 13 O2 sensor fix

faq.q: Will a Power Commander fix this?
faq.a: No — it maps fuel but won't silence OEM MIL.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit
shortDescription: Heater element inside O2 sensor not drawing current.
fullDescription:
Blink 23 indicates heater open or shorted. Sensor needs fast warm-up for accurate readings within emissions window.

Usually failed internal heater; sensor must be replaced as unit.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect under-seat fuse block for FI/O2 heater fuse.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Heater leads should read 5-15 ohms cold.

whenToCallPro: If wiring harness damage is suspected.
videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 23 O2 heater fix

faq.a: MIL will persist and fueling slower to adapt.

title: Idle Air Control Valve Fault
fullDescription:
Blink 29 indicates failure in IACV drive circuit. Idle may hunt, stall, or sit too high since ECM cannot meter bypass air correctly.

Carbon build-up inside bore is common on commuter bikes.

fixSteps.title: Remove IACV
fixSteps.instruction: Unbolt from throttle body, clean bore with TB cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Check coils
fixSteps.instruction: Each stepper winding should be ~100 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace if failed
fixSteps.instruction: Install new IACV and relearn idle.

whenToCallPro: HDS idle relearn needed on some models.
videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 29 IACV fix

title: ECM EEPROM Fault
fullDescription:
Blink 33 indicates failure to read/write ECM internal EEPROM. Often after battery surge or improper flash.

ECM may boot with defaults, bike runs poorly. In some cases re-flash resolves; otherwise replace ECM.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: If reflash fails ECM is bad.

title: Random Misfire
fullDescription:
Blink 34 means ECM detected misfires without clear pattern. Could be fuel, ignition, compression, or sensor issue.

Start with plugs/coils, then fuel pressure, then compression test.

fixSteps.title: Change plugs
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM-spec NGK plugs gapped correctly.

fixSteps.title: Check fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Rail pressure should be 43-50 psi depending on model.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 34 random misfire fix

faq.a: Yes — drain and refill if recent fill-up.

title: Bank Angle Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Lean angle/bank sensor circuit fault or tipped.
fullDescription:
Blink 54 indicates bank angle sensor tripped (bike tipped over) or sensor fault. ECM cuts spark and fuel as safety. After tipping, cycle ignition to reset.

If bike was not tipped, sensor or mounting is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Cycle ignition
fixSteps.instruction: Turn key off 10 seconds and on to reset sensor.

fixSteps.title: Check mount
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor must be mounted upright per orientation mark.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if fault persists.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 54 bank angle sensor fix

faq.q: How do I reset after drop?
faq.a: Key off then on — the sensor self-clears.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response
shortDescription: O2 sensor does not switch quickly enough.
fullDescription:
Blink 21 sets when O2 signal is sluggish. The aged sensor element fails to cross rich/lean thresholds within expected time.

Replace with OEM and verify exhaust has no leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace O2 sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM narrowband, avoid silicone sealers nearby.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Repair leaks within 12 inches of sensor.

videoSearchQuery: Honda motorcycle FI code 21 O2 slow response fix

title: Primary Coil Peak Voltage Low
shortDescription: Ignition coil primary peak voltage below threshold.
fullDescription:
Blink 91 means ECM sees coil primary peak voltage too low. Could be failing coil, low battery voltage, or shorted wiring.

Start with charging system and coil resistance checks.
